comprise of the rosary, a talk given by an invited speaker, the novena prayer and petitions (which can be placed in a box at the door of the church), a eucharistic healing ceremony and finishing with benediction of the most blessed sacrament. once again, the theme of this year’s novena is “throwing open the doors to christ” – taken from the homily of pope st john paul at the opening mass of his pontificate on 22 october 1978. the guest speaker will be chief superintendent goretti sheridan. all are very welcome. please come along, bring your families and make the most of this opportunity for prayer as we approach the season of christ’s birth. readings for all saints 1st reading: apoc 7:2-4, 9-14. the ‘apocalypse’ ‘the revelation to john’ tells of things hidden in the future. composed before 90 ad‘the book is an epic of chris- tian hope, the victory song of the perse- cuted church,’ an image of the souls al- ready in heaven. it speaks ‘of those who (will) have been through the great persecution, and have washed their robes white again in the blood of the lamb.’ 2nd reading : 1 jn 3:1-3. to be able to stand before god with confidence and joy,‘to be like him and to see him as he really is’, this is what jesus’s coming has enabled us to do. he “lets us be called god’s chil- dren…” and “surely everyone who enter- tains this hope must purify themselves, as he is pure.” submit to the will of god. god’s kingdom is the answer to the prayers of those who long for a better way than that of the world. having been through “the great persecution”, mentioned in the first reading, their “reward will be great in heaven.” wildwood 12a | 130mins sunday 1st nov - 3pm monday 2nd - wednesday 4th 8.15pm thursday 5th 5pm all saints and all souls

£757. restoration: £489. retired priests: £347. merci! all saints day and all souls day – everyone is invited to be a saint. the beatitudes gospel of all saints day (1st november) is a portrait of christ but also a portrait of a saint. the saints are those who are in heaven, already enjoying the beatific vision. those who have died and are on their way to heaven but have not yet entered it are the holy souls, whose feast is the following day (2nd november). annual mass for the dead – thursday 5th november, 7.30pm. during this mass the names of those buried in the parish in the last twelve months will be read out. one relative of each will be invited to carry forward a candle in honour of the deceased loved one. please nominate a family member and spread the word about the mass for the dead. all souls – our day of prayer for the faithful departed holy souls and saints: the catechism (ccc) teaches that immediately after death comes the particular judgement (ccc 1021). the soul has three possible paths: immediate entrance to heaven immediate entrance to purgatory to prepare for heaven immediate condemnation to hell (ccc 1022). those who are in purgatory are on their way to heaven, but they are not ready. these are the holy souls. they are perpetual friends of god because they died in the state of grace, but they must spend time in purgatory to achieve the holiness needed for heaven (ccc 1030). for this purification from sin to take place, the holy souls need the prayers of the living (ccc 1032). prayer, especially the mass, hastens their entry to heaven. we are making saints, by getting deceased people across the finish line, so to speak. this is our prayer intention for november. it’s our love for the dead. indulgences: we can name a specific soul and ask god to grant the person a shortening (partial indulgence) or a complete remission of punishment for sin (plenary indulgence). for the indulgence prayers and conditions, see the leaflets at the church ardmore parish newsletter sunday, 1st november 2026 feast of all saints remembering the saints, praying for the faithful departed feast of all saints — sunday 1st november today, 1st november, is the feast of all saints . on this day, the church celebrates all the saints: canonised or beatified, and the multitude of those who are in heaven enjoying the beatific vision that are only known to god. prayer for all saints god our father, source of all holiness, the work of your hands is manifest in your saints, the beauty of your truth is reflected in their faith. may we who aspire to have part in their joy be filled with the spirit that blessed their lives, that having shared their faith on earth we may also know their peace in your kingdom. grant this through christ, our lord. feast of all souls — monday 2nd november tomorrow, monday, on the feast of all souls , we are encouraged to remember and pray for the faithful departed, those members of our families and dearly beloved who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith. indulgences for the holy souls 1. visiting a church or oratory from 12 noon on 1st november until midnight on 2nd november , all who have confessed, received holy communion, and prayed for the pope’s intentions (one our father and hail mary, or any other prayer of one’s choice) can gain one plenary indulgence by visiting a church or oratory, and there reciting one our father and the apostles’ creed. this indulgence is applicable only to the souls of the departed. ardmore

confession may be made at any time within the week preceding or the week following 1st november. holy communion may be received on any day from 1st to 8th november. 2. visiting a cemetery the faithful who visit a cemetery and pray for the dead may gain a plenary indulgence applicable only to the holy souls on the usual conditions, once per day from 1st to 8th november . the conditions mentioned above apply also for this. prayer for all the deceased god our father, your power brings us to birth, your providence guides our lives, and by your command we return to dust. lord, those who die still live in your presence, their lives change but do not end. i pray in hope for my family, relatives and friends, and for all the dead known to you alone. in company with christ, who died and now lives, may they rejoice in your kingdom, where all our tears are wiped away. unite us together again in one family to sing your praise forever and ever. liturgy & the coming week scripture readings — sunday 8th november reading scripture first reading wisdom 6:12– 16 responsorial psalm 63:2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–8 second reading 1 thessalonians 4:13– 17 gospel matthew 25:1– 13 saints of the coming week day feast / memorial
